paragraphs.text: Designers should code, and engineers should design.

For years, titles decided who was allowed to touch what. Designers designed, engineers coded, and everything in between was a handoff: a rebuild, a round of screenshots, a backlog of small fixes nobody had time for. That handoff is where products lose their quality.
AI took away the reason to keep the roles apart. A designer with an agent can code. An engineer with an agent can design.
The best teams already work like this. The canvas is still where an idea starts. It is just not where the work stops anymore.
What does not change is who owns quality. Design owns how the product looks and feels. Engineering owns the code that ships.
So an engineer's design is an idea, and a designer makes it production ready. A designer's pull request is a start, and an engineer polishes it before it merges.
That is not a handoff. Both people work on the same thing, so nothing gets rebuilt and nothing gets lost.
Anyone can start anything now. The owner still finishes it.
